title: Finite normalization of a complete discrete valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction field $K$. Let $L/K$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], meaning finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $C\subseteq L$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], namely all elements satisfying a monic polynomial over $A$. Then $C$ is a discrete valuation ring, has fraction field $L$, is finite as an $A$-module, and is complete for its own maximal ideal. The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow C$ is local: $\mathfrak m_C\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$. Moreover, if $V\subseteq L$ is any discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$, containing $A$, and $A\hookrightarrow V$ is local in this same sense, then $V=C$. Neither separability of $L/K$ nor perfectness of the residue field of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 09EM (remark-construction, assertions (1), (4), (8)) and 09F8 (lemma-special-case, proof first paragraph: finite extensions of a complete DVR have finite complete DVR integral closure, and the given DVR equals that closure by maximality for domination); Algebra Tag 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata) supplies finiteness in the inseparable case.

proof.text: Because $A$ is a DVR, it is a principal ideal domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] it is Noetherian. It is local and complete by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] makes $A$ Nagata. Apply the definition [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] to the prime $(0)$: the domain $A/(0)=A$ is N-2. By [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], applied to the given finite extension $L/K$, its integral closure $C$ is a finite $A$-module. This uses the N-2 condition for all finite extensions, with no separability hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), 032R (definition-nagata), 032F (definition-N); More on Algebra Tag 09F8 (lemma-special-case), proof first paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] to $A$, its fraction field $K$, and $L/K$. It gives that $C$ is a domain, is integrally closed in $L$, and has fraction field $L$. The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow C$ is injective because both rings are subrings of $L$, and it is integral by the definition of $C$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Tags 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal), 0308 (lemma-integral-closure-transitive), 00GP (definition-integral-closure); More on Algebra Tag 09EM (remark-construction), first assertion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] to the finite $A$-algebra $C$. Since $C$ is a domain by Step 2, its domain clause gives that $C$ is a Noetherian local ring complete for its own maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] to $A\to C$ and this maximal ideal: its inverse image is $\mathfrak m_A$. Thus the inclusion is local, as required.

source.place: Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local), second sentence and its domain consequence; More on Algebra Tag 09F8 (lemma-special-case), proof first paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $\dim A=1$. The injective integral map $A\hookrightarrow C$ from Step 2 satisfies [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal], hence $\dim C=\dim A=1$. Steps 2 and 3 give normality, Noetherianity and locality of $C$, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] shows that $C$ is a discrete valuation ring. This also excludes the field case.

source.place: Tags 00OK (lemma-integral-sub-dim-equal) and 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), conditions (1), (3), (5); More on Algebra Tag 09EM (remark-construction), assertions (1) and (4)

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq L$ be a DVR as in the uniqueness assertion. It is a principal ideal domain [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] says that it is integrally closed in its fraction field $L$. For $c\in C$, the monic polynomial over $A$ witnessing its membership in $C$ is also a monic polynomial over $V$, since $A\subseteq V$. Thus $c$ is integral over $V$ and belongs to $V$. This proves $C\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), DVRs are PIDs and normal; More on Algebra Tag 09F8 (lemma-special-case), proof first paragraph, maximality for domination

proof.text: Choose uniformizers $\pi$ of $A$ and $t$ of $C$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. By locality in Step 3, $\pi\in\mathfrak m_C$ and $\pi\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], $\pi=u t^e$ for a unit $u\in C$ and $e\ge1$ (exponent zero would make $\pi$ a unit). In $V$ the element $\pi$ is a nonunit because $A\to V$ is local. Since $u$ stays a unit under $C\subseteq V$, $t$ cannot be a unit of $V$. Now any nonzero $x\in V\subseteq L=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ is $a/b$ with nonzero $a,b\in C$. Write $a=u_a t^r$ and $b=u_b t^s$ by the same power decomposition. If $r\ge s$, then $x=u_a u_b^{-1}t^{r-s}\in C$. If $r<s$, putting $q=s-r\ge1$ gives $t^{-1}=(u_a u_b^{-1})^{-1}x t^{q-1}\in V$, contradicting that $t$ is a nonunit there. Thus every nonzero $x\in V$ belongs to $C$, and zero does as well. Together with Step 5 this proves $V=C$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final uniformizer-power assertion; explicit DVR argument for More on Algebra Tag 09F8 (lemma-special-case), proof first paragraph, maximality for domination

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-42dd55fac (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's six steps in full, every cited statement, Stacks more-algebra 09F8 (lemma-special-case, line 35370, first paragraph of the proof) and 09EM (remark-construction, lines 33882-33957, (4) and (8)). The statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are identical to the Q132 creation record, so nothing was weakened. Its only citer, lem-per-epp-common-finite-trait-extension, is unaffected. There are no new nodes. Step 1: DVR -> PID -> Noetherian, then complete-local Nagata (032W) at the prime (0), then the N-2 definition gives module finiteness for any finite L/K, with no separability needed. Step 2: the finite-extension-normal leaf gives domain, Frac C = L and integral closedness. Step 3: the domain clause of finite-over-complete-local-product (0325) gives C local and complete for its own maximal ideal, and the finite-algebra-local-radical leaf gives the contraction to m_A. Step 4: dim A = 1, integral-injective dimension equality gives dim C = 1, and normal Noetherian local of dimension 1 gives a DVR (lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr, used only after all its hypotheses are established). Step 5: V is a PID, hence normal, so C is contained in V. Step 6: write pi = u t^e with e >= 1. t is a nonunit in V because A -> V is local. If x = a/b had r < s, then t^{-1} = (u_a u_b^{-1})^{-1} x t^{q-1} would lie in V, so x lies in C; I checked the algebra. Edge cases tested: L = K, totally ramified t = s^e, purely inseparable extensions with imperfect residue field, unramified extensions, and nonlocal overrings, which are excluded by the locality hypothesis. The proof_deps closure (191 nodes) does not contain the item, so there is no cycle. There is no SGA citation and every step is under 2000 characters. I searched for duplicates with rg over 09F8, 09EM and 'complete discrete valuation'/'dominat': the sbc compositum nodes assume separability, the l-adic node covers only Q_l, and the Nagata domination nodes are generic. None states the item. I accepted the three recorded tool_uses (sk-thm-p1 Nagata, finite-over-complete product, integral dimension equality): each is genuine generic algebra that the unit sk-p-dl-a1-perverse lacks.
